title: Change detection: zone.js, OnPush and where it is heading without zones

videos.script:
The planner's numbers change, and the page follows. Today is about how Angular knows when to redraw. {{walk}} It walks its tree of components and asks every template whether anything is different. The question is when it walks, and which components it visits.

{{zone}} For eight years the answer was a library called zone.js. It wrapped every timer, click and request in the browser, and after any of them, Angular walked everything. You add it to the planner for one section and watch a plain field update itself. {{onpush}} Then OnPush, the setting that told Angular to skip a component unless something marked it.

{{zoneless}} Then you take zone.js out again. The planner has run without it since lesson 2. The same plain field now keeps its old value, silently, and a signal does not. That is why lesson 6 came first.

{{ng0100}} You also meet an error that only development mode shows, NG0100, and learn what it is protecting you from. {{choose}} And you finish with every planner component on OnPush.
